slides.heading: Permutations
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Medium · Recursion
slides.narration: Let's solve Permutations, a medium recursion problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: All orderings of a list of distinct ints (empty input yields an empty list).
slides.narration: Here's the problem. All orderings of a list of distinct ints (empty input yields an empty list).

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Build permutations by swapping each remaining element into the current position.
slides.narration: Build permutations by swapping each remaining element into the current position.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Build by inserting into every position → O(n!·n²)
Output size n! is the true lower bound
slides.narration: Inserting each element into every position of smaller permutations works but copies a lot. Swap-based backtracking fixes one position at a time in place. Either way the output itself is n factorial.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 2. Swap each later element into position i
slides.narration: Step by step. First, recurse on index i. Second, swap each later element into position i. Third, recurse, then swap back.

slides.caption: Leaf → record [1, 2, 3]
slides.narration: All positions are fixed, so we record 1, 2, 3.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: If the array is non-empty we call permute from zero. At the last index we record a copy. Otherwise, for each j from i, swap i and j, recurse, and swap back.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n times n factorial. Space is O of n times n factorial.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
slides.narration: Always undo the swap after recursing, and copy the array when you record it, or every result ends up the same list.

slides.heading: Interview tips & follow-ups
bullets: Follow-up: duplicates → skip repeated values per position
slides.narration: With duplicates, skip values already used at a position. Next permutation is a common sibling question.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: Build permutations by swapping each remaining element into the current position.
slides.narration: To recap Permutations: Build permutations by swapping each remaining element into the current position. Try re-implementing it from scratch without looking.
